EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a strong carbonyl band at ~1700 cm⁻¹ consistent with an aromatic aldehyde, plus a prominent ring stretch near 1592 cm⁻¹. The strong band at 843 cm⁻¹ is typical of the C–H out-of-plane mode of a para-disubstituted benzene (CHO para to another substituent). Critically, the presence of two halogen-region bands at 703 and 632 cm⁻¹ supports aryl C–Cl stretching rather than C–F (which would dominate ~1000–1300 cm⁻¹). Candidate 4 (p-chlorobenzaldehyde) matches these features, while candidates with F (2) lack the C–Cl signatures, and the nitro-containing ring (9) would typically show a stronger ~1340 cm⁻¹ NO₂ symmetric stretch not observed here. The CH stretch near 3073 cm⁻¹ aligns with aromatic/aldehydic C–H (GFQ-003).
